SCIENCE · STUDENT OUTCOMES

From GCSE to A level

Explore how your students’ science grades progressed.

Local files · Private analysis

1. Import your results

One student per row, with GCSE and A-level columns for Physics, Biology and Chemistry, plus an optional Combined Science GCSE column (for example, 9–9 or 8–7). Import an .xlsx workbook.

Choose a workbook to begin.

2. Match the grade columns

Tables are generated automatically when the default columns are detected. To change a comparison, edit the columns below and choose Produce percentage matrices. You can select the same A-level column for several comparisons, for example Physics A Level for all three GCSE subjects.

Preview first five student rows

3. GCSE → A-level outcomes

Each row answers: “Of students with this GCSE grade, what percentage achieved each A-level grade?”

These are observed proportions in your imported cohort, not a prediction of an individual student’s chance. Missing and unrecognised grade pairs are excluded for each subject. GCSE 9–1 and letter grades are shown separately.
Low % in rowHighest % in rowEach row has its own scale; 0% has no colour.

Click any percentage to see the matching students and their grades. Names are taken from the first spreadsheet column.

Student records stay in your browser. Files are never uploaded. Closing or refreshing the page clears the imported results.
